filed: 2026-11-23, definition-lead (writer agent), on redteam-lead's pre-run points relayed by definition-lead; before any V1 value exists (M's scans running). predictions.json is unchanged; this file adds to it.
a_two_Ds: The control compares two Ds: x2 and x10 (and rebuilt, random_size_241001) are read on E214's copy24 held-out windows (75 x 41 tokens, all 41 read positions); new_few, new_thin and random_kl_241002 on the edits' cue windows (512 x 41, last position). A V1 gap between the two groups reads as a difference of D, not of edit, unless a reuse item is read on the cue D too. The same-D control: x2 and x10 scanned as F on the cue windows (run.py stage fcue, items reported as control_cue/x2, control_cue/x10), read against M's K on that D. Only the same-D comparison (x2, x10 on cue windows against new_few, new_thin, random_kl_241002) is read for rival A or B; the cross-D one is reported, not read.

b_expected_V1_new_edits.rule: V1 = 1 - (F's flip-mass share on K_F outside K_M). Split K_F into the variables the edit changed and the rest. The rest have M's own mechanisms (exact weight comparison), so they leave K_M only where M's run on D differs from F's enough to change which variables M needs. From E277's saved F arrays (experiments/needed_neurons/results/large/items_<item>.npz: flips, in_K, changed), the changed variables carry this share of F's flip mass: new_few 0.0345 (9 changed of |K_F| 6,032), new_thin 0.4175 (1,279 changed of 2,882); x2 0.0027, x10 0.0025 (9 changed each), random_kl_241002 1.0 (every variable changed).
b_expected_V1_new_edits.expected: If K_M holds every unchanged member of K_F (M and F differ only through the edit), V1 is 1 - (the changed variables' share outside K_M), so V1(new_few) lies in [0.966, 1] and V1(new_thin) in [0.583, 1]: the low end when no changed variable is in K_M, 1 when the edit runs through variables M also needs. x2 and x10 under the same assumption lie in [0.997, 1]. So on new_few, V1 cannot fall 0.2 below x2 and x10 unless M fails to need unchanged variables F needs (a difference of D's outputs, not of the edit); new_thin can, by at most 0.42, and only if its changed variables lie outside K_M. random_kl_241002: no bound from construction (every variable changed).
b_expected_V1_new_edits.consequence: Rival A's control can be met only through new_thin and random_kl_241002, never through new_few, unless unchanged variables leave K_M. This was derivable before the run and is recorded so a V1 reading near 1 on new_few is not read as a finding.

c_control_margin: Rival A's control is read with the card's smallest_gap 0.2: min over x2 and x10 at least 0.2 above max over new_few, new_thin and random_kl_241002, on the same D (a above), on each of V1 and V2 separately. Below that, rival B's pattern (no separation). This replaces predictions.json rules '(1) control''s comparison with no margin.
d_V2_measures_update_size: V2 at f = 0.25 is recorded as measuring the size of the update per variable, not reliance: a small update leaves nearly every variable's write within half of M's own, so V2 sits near 1 for any small fine-tune or random update whatever it does (v2_preview.json, committed 2a68495b after predictions.json, already showed this; the point is recorded here as redteam-lead raised it before V1).
added_columns: score.py also reports, beside V1, the unweighted overlap |K_F and K_M| / |K_F| (overlap) and |K_M| (size_K_M) for every item: descriptive, no rule.
